parsed.rationale: Both `ArtistRepository` and `ReleaseRepository` in the `Metadata` package share three identical members — `cacheKey:(for id: Int) -> String`, `entityKind:String`, and `lastSync:Date?` — and differ only in the return type of their `resolve:(id: Int) async throws -> <Entity>` method (`Artist` vs `Release`). This is the canonical PAT pattern: a family of protocols that are structurally identical except for one varying concrete type. Introducing a `Repository` protocol with `associatedtype Entity` and moving the four members onto it (with `resolve` typed as `(id: Int) async throws -> Entity`) eliminates the duplication while preserving full type safety for each conformer. Neither record carries any restraint marker (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so no restraint rule applies.
